assign() and markDone(): catch errors from the use cases and turn them into HTTP 400 JSON responses. This is error handling at the transport boundary.
list(): reads route and query parameters into ListTasksFilter and leaves the filtering to listTasksUseCase.
taskToDTO(): converts a domain Task to a serialisable TaskDTO for the response. This is presentation mapping and contains no business rule.

parsedVerdict.reasoning: TaskController is an Express HTTP adapter in the infrastructure layer. It only does transport work. It reads req.body, req.params and req.query, and checks that required fields are present. It converts the transport strings it receives: it parses dueDate into a Date and narrows the query string into ListTasksFilter. It hands off to the application use cases and turns caught errors into HTTP 400 responses. It sets status codes such as 201, and it converts domain Task objects into the response TaskDTO. It contains no business rules: assignment and completion rules stay inside the use cases. It has no persistence logic either. Mapping the domain object to a response DTO inside an adapter is normal presentation work. One could argue that taskToDTO belongs in the application layer, because TaskDTO is defined there. Even so, building the response shape is the adapter's job, so it is not a misplaced responsibility of a different layer kind.
